label: Cognition
description: A persona's day with a live LLM: generate a plan (day -> hourly -> minute), seed beliefs + plan into memory, then each step perceive, retrieve, decide, maybe converse, remember, and periodically reflect. Click a node to read its prompt. With the default mock brain the blue prompts aren't sent (the mock decides from location alone), but the green memory text is still written.

frontmatter.name: plan_system
frontmatter.description: System message for the LLM daily planner (backend/planner.py, LLMPlanner, issue #83). Shared across the three-level decomposition -- day outline -> hourly -> minute stops -- and the revise pass. Unlike the other gen-agents templates (which hold memory content), this IS a real model prompt: it tells the model to plan in character for a Smallville resident. The per-level user message (persona text, memory block, hour window, prior level) is assembled in code, like other observation scaffolding (issue #145).

frontmatter.name: plan_memory
frontmatter.description: The day's PLAN memory seeded onto each Smallville persona at t=0 (backend/smallville_agents.py, attach_agents). It is the agent's own private intention -- "go to <destination> and <activity>", plus the day's full itinerary -- distinct from its persona, so retrieval has the agent's whole plan to surface from turn 0 and the PLAN memory kind is exercised. The deterministic mock brain never reads it (it decides from location alone); real retrieval would surface it.

destination.description: The first place the persona plans to go, e.g. "Hobbs Cafe".

activity.description: What the persona plans to do there, e.g. "tending the cafe counter".

itinerary.description: The whole day's stops, pre-joined as "<activity> at <place>, then ..." (see attach_agents). Optional; the "Today's stops" sentence is dropped when it's empty.

sample.itinerary: tending the cafe counter at Hobbs Cafe, then reading at the library

frontmatter.name: npc_decision
frontmatter.description: System message for an LLM-driven NPC's ReAct decision (text_adventure_games/npc.py, LLMAgent). Renders the persona and goals, and -- on the free-text path -- the labeled Reasoning/Action/Duration instruction. The structured tool-calling path renders the same persona/goals block but omits the instruction, because there the tool schema is the output contract. The character's name is deliberately left out: identity rides on the first-person persona, and the observation already names the scene and everyone in it, so the model speaks as "I" without being told its own name.

persona.description: First-person persona string. The Persona line is dropped when empty.

goals_block.description: Pre-formatted goals grouped by tier (see LLMAgent._format_goals). The Goals section is dropped when empty.

include_instruction.description: True on the free-text path (append the ReAct instruction); False on the structured tool-calling path (omit it).

reasoning_label.description: The reasoning line label, e.g. "Reasoning:" (from ReActLabel).

action_label.description: The action line label, e.g. "Action:" (from ReActLabel).

duration_label.description: The duration line label, e.g. "Duration:" (from ReActLabel).

sample.persona: I am the troll. I guard the drawbridge.
sample.goals_block:
Short-term:
  - keep the player off the bridge

decide.rendered:
You are an NPC in a text adventure game.
Persona: I am Diego Torres, a graduate student in architecture at Penn. I spend long hours in the Meyerson Hall studio.
Goals:
Short-term:
  - work on the studio model in Meyerson Hall
Based on your persona, goals, and the current situation, choose a single game command to execute. Reply with exactly three lines:
Reasoning: <one short sentence explaining your choice>
Action: <the command, e.g. 'attack player', 'go north', 'take sword'>
Duration: <estimated in-game minutes this action takes, e.g. 5>

frontmatter.name: npc_dialogue
frontmatter.description: System message for an LLM-driven NPC speaking a line in a conversation (text_adventure_games/npc.py, LLMAgent._dialogue_system_message, issue #86). Renders the same persona/goals block as npc_decision, then the one-line dialogue instruction (the conversation asks for one utterance at a time; the agent bows out with a brief goodbye when the talk has run its course). The character's name is deliberately left out: identity rides on the first-person persona, and the dialogue observation already names the partner.

persona.description: First-person persona string. The Persona line is dropped when empty.

goals_block.description: Pre-formatted goals grouped by tier (see LLMAgent._format_goals). The Goals section is dropped when empty.

dialogue.rendered:
You are an NPC in a text adventure game.
Persona: I am Diego Torres, a graduate student in architecture at Penn. I spend long hours in the Meyerson Hall studio.
You are in a conversation. Reply with the single line you say next, in character. Keep it to a sentence or two. If the conversation has reached a natural end, say a brief goodbye.

frontmatter.name: reflection
frontmatter.description: A persona's own successful action, recorded as a first-person observation memory (backend/smallville_agents.py, remember_outcome). The command verb selects the phrasing: arriving somewhere, doing an activity, or a quoted fallback for any other command. The memory's importance is chosen in Python (it is data, not text), so only the wording lives here.

verb.description: The command verb -- "travel", "perform", or anything else.

location.description: The place arrived at (used when verb == "travel").

activity.description: What the persona is doing (used when verb == "perform").

command.description: The raw command, quoted verbatim in the fallback (any other verb).

reflect.description: reflection.reflect() / LLMReflector (#84) -- when accumulated importance crosses a threshold, synthesize higher-level insights from recent memories. Real model call (live client only); the numbered memory window rides in the user message.

frontmatter.name: reflect_system
frontmatter.description: System message for LLM-driven periodic reflection (text_adventure_games/ reflection.py, LLMReflector). Shared by both reflection steps -- asking for the salient high-level questions a window of memories raises, and inferring one grounded insight per question. The per-call user message (the numbered memory window + the step instruction) is assembled in code, like other observation scaffolding (issue #145).

reflect.raw_source: You are reflecting on your own recent experiences to form higher-level insights about yourself, the people around you, and your situation. Ground every insight only in the memories you are given.
reflect.rendered: You are reflecting on your own recent experiences to form higher-level insights about yourself, the people around you, and your situation. Ground every insight only in the memories you are given.
